questions.text: Is the company established (registered or with a place of establishment) in the EU?

questions.help: Headcount and annual turnover, as in the EU definition of SMEs.
Pre-fills the area of use of each new AI system.

questions.text: Describe the sector in your own words (optional)
questions.help: For example "education technology for secondary schools".

questions.text: Does the company develop AI systems, or build AI into products or services it offers under its own name?
Are those systems or products placed on the market, put into service or offered in the EU?
Does the company use AI systems in its work, including third-party tools such as chatbots, copilots, scoring or screening tools?
Is the output of the company's AI systems used in the EU?
Does the company import or resell AI systems made by others in the EU?
Does the company process personal data (about customers, staff or anyone else)?

sections.title: Other EU digital regulations
sections.intro: Not covered by the Hub yet. If one applies, a SenecAI consultant can help you assess and implement it.

questions.text: Does the company operate in any of these sectors? Tick all that apply, or none.

options.label: Energy (electricity, gas, oil, district heating, hydrogen)
Digital infrastructure (cloud, data centres, DNS, telecoms, trust services)
Managed IT or security services for other businesses
Online marketplaces, search engines or social networks
Manufacturing of electronics, machinery, vehicles or medical devices

questions.text: Is the company a financial entity, such as a bank, payment or e-money institution, investment firm, insurer or crypto-asset service provider, or does it provide ICT services to one?
Does the company make, import or sell hardware or software products that connect to a device or a network, for example connected devices, apps or installable software?
questions.help: Purely online services (software as a service) are generally not covered, unless they are part of such a product.

questions.text: Does the company make connected products that collect data about their use (for example smart devices, connected cars or machines), provide services that work with them, or offer cloud or other data processing services?

rules.rationale: The company develops AI and places it on the market or puts it into service in the EU, so it is in scope as a provider wherever it is established.
The company is established in the EU and uses AI systems professionally, so it is in scope as a deployer.
The company is established outside the EU but the output of its AI systems is used in the EU, so it is in scope.
The company imports or distributes AI systems in the EU, so it is in scope.

findings.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
findings.summary: Applies. The AI inventory and classification are opened for this client.

rules.rationale: At least one AI Act scope test applies.

findings.name: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
findings.summary: No AI Act scope test applies on these answers. Re-run the check if the company starts building, using or reselling AI.

rules.rationale: No AI Act scope test applies on these answers. If the company starts building, using or reselling AI, run the check again.

findings.name: GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)
findings.summary: Applies to the processing of personal data. Not covered by the Hub in this version.

rules.rationale: The company processes personal data, so the GDPR applies to that processing.

findings.name: NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555)
findings.summary: Likely applies. Not covered by the Hub yet, but a SenecAI consultant can help you assess it and put it in place.

rules.rationale: A medium or large company in a sector of NIS2 Annex I or II, or a provider of certain digital infrastructure of any size, is likely in scope as transposed nationally.

findings.name: DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554)
findings.summary: Likely applies. Not covered by the Hub yet, but a SenecAI consultant can help you assess it and put it in place.

rules.rationale: Financial entities listed in Art. 2(1), and ICT third-party service providers to them, are within DORA's digital operational resilience rules.

findings.name: Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847)
findings.summary: Likely applies. Not covered by the Hub yet, but a SenecAI consultant can help you assess it and put it in place.

rules.rationale: Products with digital elements made available on the EU market fall within the Cyber Resilience Act.

findings.name: Data Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/2854)
findings.summary: Likely applies. Not covered by the Hub yet, but a SenecAI consultant can help you assess it and put it in place.

rules.rationale: Manufacturers of connected products, providers of related services and providers of data processing services are within the Data Act.
